title: 🎓 The University of California gives 300,000 students and staff ChatGPT for free — and professors object!
body: 🎓 The University of California gives 300,000 students and staff ChatGPT for free — and professors object!

The University of California has expanded its agreement with OpenAI to include all its students, professors and staff across its ten campuses, under an annual contract worth $1.2 million, giving them free access to ChatGPT Edu and the Codex coding tool, with stronger protection for their data and lower costs for the university.

The new agreement starts next December. It is an extension of an earlier agreement from 2024, and also includes AI literacy workshops and professional training for students, but it excludes the university's hospitals and medical centres. The university stresses that it does not force anyone to use these tools, and that professors have complete freedom to decide on their use in their lectures.

But faculty leaders objected to the deal, saying it was concluded quickly without sufficient academic consultation, and warning of its effects on academic integrity and the quality of education, while the university administration believes every student deserves a chance to develop AI skills regardless of their background or resources.
Simply put: free AI for every student at the largest public university in America. Will ChatGPT become a basic study tool like the university textbook, or a danger to independent thinking?
